current_affected_interface_subjects.current_statement: Adopt the ideal-clock and ideal-light assumptions of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and the SI conventions of def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions. Let x: I -> A be a future timelike worldline (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline) with proper-time function tau (def-sr-proper-time), and let s_- < s_+ be parameter values. Suppose an event q and the events e_- := x(s_-), e_+ := x(s_+) satisfy: q - e_- is future null and e_+ - q is future null (def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors, def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets). Under the adopted ideal-light assumption an ideal ray is emitted at e_-, reaches q, and an ideal ray emitted at q reaches e_+; the event q is idealized as an instantaneous reflection that changes nothing else. The radar protocol of the observer assigns to q (i) the radar time tau_rad(q) := (tau(s_-)+tau(s_+))/2, the ideal clock's reading midway between emission and reception, and (ii) the radar distance rho_rad(q) := c(tau(s_+)-tau(s_-))/2, half the round-trip light time multiplied by c. Two events measured by the same observer are radar-simultaneous when their radar times agree. The assignment does not change under increasing reparametrizations of the observer's worldline, because tau does not (lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance). Conventions and scope: (a) the protocol is a definition of an operational assignment conditional on the existence of the emission, reflection and reception events, and it assumes an available ideal reflector and ideal apparatus; (b) the split of the round trip into a 'time' and a 'distance' uses the symmetric convention in which half of the round-trip time is assigned to the outgoing and half to the returning segment; the protocol determines the round-trip quantity tau(s_+)-tau(s_-) operationally, while the derived one-way assignment is a convention and does not measure a one-way light speed independently of a synchronization convention; (c) nothing is claimed about accelerated observers, dispersive or absorbing media, finite-resolution apparatus, global single-valuedness or detector models, and no measurement outcome, statistical inference or empirical comparison is asserted.
current_affected_interface_subjects.current_strategy: Definition item with formulation obligations. (i) The assigned quantities are defined from the proper-time function and the events; the stated existence hypotheses make them well defined, and invariance under increasing reparametrization is lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance. (ii) The two null segments are the operational content of the adopted ideal-light assumption (post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light); the reflection is an idealization, so the definition does not describe a physical mirror. (iii) The symmetric half-split is stated as a convention, not derived; its consequences for inertial observers are proved in pthm-sr-radar-synchronization-of-inertial-observers below, and the failure of global ring synchronization for rotating observers is exhibited by the explicit example on this page. (iv) No proof is manufactured: the item introduces an operational assignment, and its only mathematical content is well-definedness. The scope clause carries the idealizations of the postulates to every consumer.

current_affected_interface_subjects.current_statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $x:I\to A$ be a $C^1$ future timelike worldline with proper-time function $\tau:I\to J$ and inverse $\rho:J\to I$ ([[def-sr-proper-time]], [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]).
(a) For a $C^1$ map $P:I\to V$ define its proper-time derivative $\dot P:I\to V$ by
$$\dot P(s):=\frac{P'(s)}{\tau'(s)},$$
where $P'$ is the derivative of $P$ with respect to the worldline parameter, taken componentwise in any affine basis of $V$; the result does not depend on the basis because two affine bases differ by a constant invertible linear map. Equivalently $\dot P(s)=(P\circ\rho)'(\tau(s))$, so $\dot P$ is the derivative of the proper-time parametrised field $P\circ\rho$. Since $\tau'(s)>0$ by [[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]], $\dot P$ is well defined and continuous whenever $P$ is $C^1$.
(b) If $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant and $U$ the four-velocity of $x$ ([[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), then $F:=\dot P$ is called the four-force on the particle; in an inertial frame $F$ has the components of the derivative of the four-momentum with respect to proper time.
(c) This item introduces a derivative and a name only. It asserts no force law, no field equation, no equation of motion and no existence or uniqueness of solutions; the identities satisfied by $F$ for a stipulated four-momentum field are proved in [[lem-sr-four-force-and-work-energy-identities]], and a physical force law requires a further model premise.
current_affected_interface_subjects.current_strategy: Definition item. Obligations: (i) the division by $\tau'$ is legitimate because $\tau'>0$ ([[lem-sr-proper-time-parametrization]]); (ii) the equivalence $\dot P(s)=(P\circ\rho)'(\tau(s))$ is the chain rule along the reparametrisation, $\rho$ being the inverse of the increasing function $\tau$; (iii) componentwise differentiation in one affine basis and change of basis commute because the transition map is constant and linear, so the definition is basis-free; (iv) no dynamics is imported: $F$ is a derived vector field attached to a given $P$, not a prescribed law. No choice principle is used.

current_affected_interface_subjects.current_statement: Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework, extending the ideal-clock reading rule of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light to the general worldline calculus of this page: (i) Free trajectories. A massive test particle that is subject to no interaction (a free particle) has as its worldline a straight future timelike line of the affine model: there are an event p in A and a future timelike vector v in V with x(s) = p + (s - s_0) v for all s (the kinematical consequences of this shape for the four-velocity are derived, not assumed, in pthm-sr-four-velocity-norm-and-orthogonality). Interactions, forces and collisions are not part of this assumption: a particle that is not free may have any future timelike worldline admitted by its own dynamical model, and no force law is adopted here. (ii) Clock hypothesis. An ideal clock carried along a future timelike worldline of the model, including an accelerated one and a piecewise C^1 one with finitely many kinks, reads between any two parameter values the proper-time difference of def-sr-proper-time for C^1 histories and of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time for weak piecewise C^1 histories, with no additional term depending on acceleration, jerk or any higher derivative; a kink is an idealization of a finite short acceleration phase whose contribution is included through the integral on the smooth pieces, and the reading does not depend on an increasing regular change of parameter admitted by the curve definition: its derivatives on smooth pieces and all finite one-sided endpoint derivatives are positive, as in lem-sr-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance and lem-sr-piecewise-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance. Zero-tangent compositions are not worldlines of this model. (iii) Scope and qualification. The assumptions concern ideal point particles, ideal clocks and flat classical spacetime. They are adopted, not proved; they are not consequences of the affine geometry, and no experiment is claimed here to establish them. They inherit the idealizations of post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light: real clocks have finite resolution, calibration and apparatus limitations, and real particles are not exactly free.
current_affected_interface_subjects.current_strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it fixes the physical interpretation of straight future timelike lines as the histories of free massive test particles and makes the clock-reading rule applicable to the general worldline class of this page. Obligations: (i) straight future timelike lines are declared objects of the affine model, and each is a future timelike worldline with constant tangent (def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline); (ii) the reading rule is an identification of a physical clock reading with the mathematical proper-time difference, so def-sr-proper-time and its reparametrization invariance are the mathematical suppliers carrying the content, while the identification itself is adopted; (iii) the free-trajectory clause is deliberately silent about interactions and force laws, so it cannot be used to infer conservation laws, mass-shell relations or collision kinematics, which require the separate momentum postulate of the later energy-momentum page; (iv) the clock hypothesis is the assertion that ideal clocks have no acceleration-dependent term, so it must not be presented as following from the geometry. No proof is manufactured; the item is an adopted premise with an exact scope. The weak piecewise mathematical referent is supplied by def-sr-piecewise-proper-time and its integrability lemma, and regular increasing weak-piecewise parameter independence by lem-sr-piecewise-proper-time-reparametrization-invariance. This repairs the formulation of the already adopted clock assumption; it does not derive clock behavior or extend its empirical scope.

current_affected_interface_subjects.current_statement: Let c > 0 and let x: [a,b] -> A be a future timelike worldline with a < b that is piecewise C^1 with partition a = s_0 < s_1 < ... < s_m = b in the weak sense of def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline, with total proper time Delta tau(x) of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time. Put p := x(a), q := x(b) and T := sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)), a positive real number (lem-sr-endpoint-displacement-of-a-future-timelike-worldline). Then: (i) Endpoint bound: c Delta tau(x) <= T. (ii) Equality case: c Delta tau(x) = T if and only if x is a strictly increasing reparametrization of the straight segment from p to q, that is: there is a continuous strictly increasing surjection sigma: [a,b] -> [0,1] with sigma(a) = 0 and sigma(b) = 1, C^1 on every open piece of a finite weak piecewise partition of [a,b], with sigma'(s) > 0 at every point of each open piece and finite positive one-sided difference-quotient derivatives at both endpoints of every piece, without any requirement that sigma' extend continuously there, such that x(s) = p + sigma(s)(q - p) for every s in [a,b]; equivalently x'(s) is a positive multiple of q - p at every point at which x is differentiable. (iii) Strictness: if the image of x is not contained in the straight segment {p + lambda(q-p) : 0 <= lambda <= 1}, then c Delta tau(x) < T; in particular, if x is piecewise inertial and its piece tangents d_1,...,d_m are not all positive multiples of one another (equivalently, its image is not contained in the straight segment), then the inequality is strict, while a piecewise inertial itinerary whose piece tangents are all positive multiples of one another has the straight segment as image and attains the bound. (iv) Straight worldlines attain the bound: for the inertial worldline x_s(s) := p + ((s-a)/(b-a))(q-p) one has c Delta tau(x_s) = T, in agreement with the straight-segment value of def-sr-proper-time; more generally every worldline whose image is the straight segment and which is traversed in the future direction attains the bound. (v) Scope: the theorem concerns the affine Minkowski model with a fixed positive constant c; it is a statement about the weak piecewise C^1 future timelike class, including the ordinary Riemann special case (H), it does not identify proper time with any clock reading, and it asserts nothing about maximality of geodesics in curved spacetimes or in Lorentzian manifolds with different global structure.
current_affected_interface_subjects.current_strategy: By lem-sr-endpoint-displacement-of-a-future-timelike-worldline, d=q-p is future timelike and T=sqrt(-eta(d,d))>0. Choose the rest inertial frame with e0=d/T by lem-sr-rest-frame-of-a-future-timelike-displacement; the coordinate endpoint increment is (T,0,0,0). On each open piece xi=(xi0,z) has xi0'>|z'|. Put f=sqrt((xi0')^2-|z'|^2) and h=xi0'-f>=0. The integrability lemma gives finite improper integrals of xi0', f and h, the exact coordinate endpoint increment, and subdivision additivity. Hence c Delta tau=sum_i integral f<=sum_i integral xi0'=T. For equality the finite nonnegative sum of integrals h is zero, so every such integral is zero. If h were positive anywhere in an open piece, continuity would give a compact interior neighborhood of positive integral, contradiction. Therefore z'=0 inside every piece. The zero-derivative theorem and continuity at the corners make z constant throughout, while xi0'>0 implies strict time increase. Set sigma(s)=(xi0(s)-xi0(a))/T. Then sigma is continuous, strictly increasing, onto [0,1], C1 with positive derivative on every open piece, and has finite positive one-sided quotient derivatives at the corners because x does and those tangents now lie along d. This gives x=p+sigma d. Conversely that displayed weak parametrization has density T sigma' and the integrability lemma gives sum_i integral sigma'=sigma(b)-sigma(a)=1, attaining T. This proves (i)-(ii). Clause (iii) follows because a history outside the straight segment fails the equality case; for piecewise inertial histories the constant tangents are all positive multiples exactly when all legs have the same future line, and then the image is the full endpoint segment. Clause (iv) is the constant derivative d/(b-a) calculation or the equality case with affine sigma. Clause (v) preserves purely affine mathematical scope and all prior (H) special cases; no clock reading, curved-spacetime maximality or choice principle is introduced.

current_affected_interface_subjects.current_statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space with the reachability objects <=, <, J^+, I^+ and R^+ of def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space. (a) Displacement of a future causal path. Let a < b be real numbers and let x: [a,b] -> A be a piecewise C^1 future causal path with D := x(b) - x(a). Then D is in Cbar^+. If x has a future timelike one-sided tangent at some point of [a,b], then D is in C^+. If x is nonconstant, then D is not 0. (b) Reachability and straight segments. J^+(p) = R^+(p), and for q not p one has q in J^+(p) if and only if the straight path s |-> p + s(q - p), s in [0,1], is a future causal path; moreover I^+(p) = {q : the straight path from p to q is future timelike} = {q : q is reachable from p by a piecewise C^1 future causal path having a future timelike one-sided tangent at some point}, and p is in neither of these two sets. (c) No causal loops. If p <= q and q <= p then p = q; equivalently there is no nonconstant piecewise C^1 future causal path x: [a,b] -> A with x(b) = x(a). (d) Time monotonicity. For the chart x of every inertial frame and every piecewise C^1 future causal path y: [a,b] -> A, the composition x^0 o y is nondecreasing, and if y is nonconstant on a subinterval [a',b'] of [a,b] then (x^0 o y)(b') > (x^0 o y)(a'); in particular every inertial frame agrees that a nonconstant future causal path does not go backwards in coordinate time. (e) Straight-worldline maximum. Let p,q be events with q in I^+(p), put D := q - p and T := sqrt(-eta(D,D)) > 0. Then for every piecewise C^1 future timelike worldline y: [a,b] -> A with y(a) = p and y(b) = q, the elapsed proper time Delta tau(y)=c^{-1} sum_i integral_(a_i,b_i) sqrt(-eta(y',y')), defined by the finite improper-piece sum of def-sr-piecewise-proper-time on the weak C^1 pieces a = a_1 < b_1 = a_2 < ... < b_m = b, is at most T/c; equality holds if and only if the image of y is the straight segment from p to q and y traverses it with a strictly increasing time coordinate, i.e. y is a strictly increasing reparametrization of s |-> p + sD. (f) Invariance. For every proper orthochronous affine Lorentz map F of the model one has F(J^+(p)) = J^+(F(p)) and F(I^+(p)) = I^+(F(p)) for every event p, and p <= q if and only if F(p) <= F(q) for all events p,q. (g) Scope. The theorem concerns the affine model: it attaches no physical interpretation to <=, J^+, I^+ and R^+, asserts nothing about partial differential equations, propagation of particular fields or differentiability beyond piecewise C^1, and uses no choice principle.
current_affected_interface_subjects.current_strategy: Proof in dependency order; (a)-(d) are integral inequalities, (e) is the same inequality after a boost normalization, (f) is the cone invariance of a proper orthochronous Lorentz map. (a) Fix an inertial chart. By lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability, all coordinate derivatives are absolutely improperly integrable and their finite sums equal D, with D0>=|D_spatial|. The lemma's strictness clause covers both an interior timelike tangent and a timelike one-sided quotient tangent at a corner, without derivative-limit continuity. A regular future causal path has D0>0; more generally D0=0 implies every nonnegative interior time derivative is zero: any positive value would by continuity have a compact positive neighborhood and force a positive time increment. Then |z'|<=y0'=0 on every open piece, so every coordinate is constant on the pieces and endpoint continuity makes the complete path constant. This repairs the D0=0 inference explicitly; spatial vanishing alone does not prove time vanishing. (b) q in J^+(p) with q not p means D in Cbar^+ with D not 0; the straight path s |-> p + sD has constant tangent D (def-derivative, def-affine-space-and-displacement), which is future causal and nonzero, so it is a future causal path; conversely a future causal straight path has nonzero future causal tangent D, so D is in Cbar^+; this proves R^+(p) = J^+(p) and the straight-segment criterion. For I^+(p): if D is in C^+, the straight path is a future causal path with future timelike tangent, so I^+(p) is contained in the second set; conversely, if a piecewise C^1 future causal path from p to q has a future timelike tangent, then (a) gives D in C^+, so q is in I^+(p); and no closed future causal path can have a timelike tangent because its displacement would have to lie in C^+ intersect {0}. (c) If p <= q and q <= p then q - p lies in Cbar^+ intersect (Cbar^-) = {0} by def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets, so p = q; a nonconstant closed future causal path would give D = 0 with nonconstant path, contradicting (a). (d) Apply (a) to the restriction of y to [a',b'] for arbitrary a' <= b'; the displacement has nonnegative time coordinate by (a) and the second clause of (a) with (b) of lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion gives strict positivity exactly for nonconstant restrictions. (e) Let x be an inertial chart and let v := D/T (in V), a future unit timelike vector with coordinates (v^0,v_s), v^0 > 0 and |v_s| < v^0 (lem-sr-future-causal-sums-and-inertial-coordinate-criterion(a)); put beta := v_s/v^0 in R^3, so |beta| = |v_s|/v^0 < 1, and let B(beta) be the passive boost of def-lorentz-boost. Then B(beta)v = e_0: indeed B(beta) is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map (lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse, def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group), so B(beta)v is future unit timelike with time coordinate gamma(v^0 - beta . v_s) = gamma((v^0)^2 - |v_s|^2)/v^0 = gamma/v^0 = 1, since gamma = (1 - |beta|^2)^{-1/2} = v^0 by the unit identity, hence B(beta)v = e_0 and B(beta)D = T e_0. Let x_1 be the chart of the inertial frame whose ordered basis is e'_a := B(beta)^{-1} e_a (a valid eta-orthonormal, future and positively oriented basis because B(beta)^{-1} is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map, def-linear-isomorphism-and-invertible-linear-map, thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis): then x_1 = B(beta) o x up to translation and x_1(q) - x_1(p) = T e_0 with coordinates (T,0,0,0). The chart change is an affine map whose linear part is a Lorentz map, so it preserves eta: eta(y',y') = eta(y_1',y_1') for the coordinate paths, and it preserves the future direction of timelike tangents; hence y_1' is future timelike, its time coordinate is positive, and pointwise sqrt((y_1'^0)^2 - |y_1'_s|^2) <= y_1'^0 with equality exactly when y_1'_s = 0 (elementary inequality for 0 <= |b| <= a: sqrt(a^2 - b^2) <= a with equality iff b = 0). By lem-sr-weak-piecewise-causal-integrability and def-sr-piecewise-proper-time, the finite improper-piece sum gives c Delta tau(y)=sum_i integral f_i<=sum_i integral y1'^0=x1^0(q)-x1^0(p)=T. Thus Delta tau(y)<=T/c, with exactly one conversion factor c^{-1}. Each integral is first taken on proper interior truncations and then passed to its finite endpoint limits. For equality put h_i=y1'^0-f_i>=0 on each open piece; it is continuous and dominated by y1'^0, hence improperly integrable. Equality forces every integral h_i to vanish. If h_i were positive at an interior point, continuity would give a compact interval with positive integral, contradicting that vanishing. Hence every spatial derivative vanishes on every open piece. Zero-derivative constancy and endpoint continuity give a constant spatial coordinate throughout; the positive time derivative makes the time coordinate strictly increasing, so y(s)=p+sigma(s)D with sigma continuous, strictly increasing and onto [0,1], C1 on open pieces and with finite positive one-sided quotient derivatives inherited from y. Conversely such a worldline has density T sigma', and its improper integral telescopes by the supplier lemma to T(sigma(b)-sigma(a))=T. This proves the bound and exact equality case for the approved weak class, retaining every straight attainment conclusion. (f) If F(p) = F(p_0) + L(p - p_0) with L proper orthochronous (def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group), then F(p + Cbar^+) = F(p) + L(Cbar^+) = F(p) + Cbar^+ because L preserves the future and past closed cones (thm-sr-proper-orthochronous-lorentz-algebra(iv)), which is exactly F(J^+(p)) = J^+(F(p)) and likewise for C^+ and I^+; the relation form follows. No choice principle is used: the arguments are finite-dimensional coordinate calculus, one explicit boost and ordinary integrals on compact interior truncations and finite improper endpoint limits.

current_affected_interface_subjects.current_statement: Let c > 0 and let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space. (a) Norm of the four-velocity. Let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration). Then eta(U(s),U(s)) = -c^2 for every s in I; equivalently the dimensionless four-velocity u = U/c satisfies eta(u,u) = -1, and U(s) is future timelike. Thus the four-velocity of a worldline lies on the future unit hyperboloid. (b) Orthogonality of the four-acceleration. If x is C^2 at s, then eta(U(s),A(s)) = 0: the four-acceleration has no component along the four-velocity; if in addition A(s) is nonzero, then A(s) is spacelike. (c) Rest space and projection. Let n in V be future unit timelike, eta(n,n) = -1, and put n^perp := {v in V : eta(n,v) = 0}. Then n^perp is a 3-dimensional linear subspace of V, the restriction of eta to n^perp is positive definite, and the map h: V -> V, h(v) := v + eta(n,v) n, is linear, idempotent with h o h = h, has image n^perp and kernel span(n), satisfies h(n) = 0 and eta(n,h(v)) = 0 for all v in V, and every v in V has the unique decomposition v = -eta(n,v) n + h(v). Moreover |w| := sqrt(eta(w,w)) defines a norm on n^perp. (d) Relative velocity and Lorentz factor. Let n and u be future unit timelike vectors, put gamma := -eta(n,u) and w := c h(u)/gamma. Then gamma >= 1, w lies in n^perp, u = gamma (n + w/c), |w|^2 = c^2 (1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and gamma = 1 if and only if u = n. The vector w is the velocity of a worldline with four-velocity c u relative to the observer n and gamma is its Lorentz factor. (e) Coordinate form. Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame and let y be a C^1 future timelike worldline whose inertial coordinates are t |-> (c t, r(t)), with coordinate velocity w(t) := r'(t) in R^3 and, when y is C^2, coordinate acceleration a(t) := w'(t). Then |w(t)| < c, the four-velocity is U = gamma_w (c,w) with gamma_w := (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and the four-acceleration is A = gamma_w (d/dt)(gamma_w (c,w)), so that A^0 = gamma_w^4 (w.a)/c and A_vec = gamma_w^2 a + gamma_w^4 (w.a) w/c^2; consequently eta(A,A) = gamma_w^4 |a|^2 + gamma_w^6 (w.a)^2/c^2 >= 0, with eta(A,A) = 0 if and only if a = 0, and eta(U,A) = 0. For the observer n = e_0 of the chart, clauses (c) and (d) specialize to gamma = gamma_w and w_rel = w. (f) Scope. The statement is a theorem about the affine Minkowski model with a fixed positive constant c; it asserts no clock reading and identifies no physical four-velocity. No choice principle is used.
current_affected_interface_subjects.current_strategy: Proof in dependency order; the hard part is (c), which is pure algebra plus one coordinate computation, and the remaining clauses follow from it. (c) Fix an eta-orthonormal basis with e_0 timelike (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis; use an inertial frame of def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Write n = n^0 e_0 + n_s and v = v^0 e_0 + v_s with n_s,v_s in S = span(e_1,e_2,e_3), where eta restricts to the positive definite delta with norm |.| (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame). From eta(n,n) = -(n^0)^2 + |n_s|^2 = -1 one gets (n^0)^2 = 1 + |n_s|^2 > 0. For v with eta(n,v) = -n^0 v^0 + delta(n_s,v_s) = 0 one has v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0, hence eta(v,v) = -(v^0)^2 + |v_s|^2 = |v_s|^2 - delta(n_s,v_s)^2/(n^0)^2 >= |v_s|^2 (1 - |n_s|^2/(n^0)^2) = |v_s|^2/(n^0)^2 >= 0 by the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for delta (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite); equality forces |v_s| = 0 and then v^0 = 0, so v = 0 and the restriction is positive definite. The map v_s |-> v^0 e_0 + v_s with v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0 is a linear bijection S -> n^perp, so n^perp is 3-dimensional. The properties of h are immediate from bilinearity of eta (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia, def-linear-map): eta(n,h(v)) = eta(n,v) + eta(n,v)eta(n,n) = 0, so h(v) lies in n^perp; h(n) = n + eta(n,n)n = 0; h(h(v)) = h(v) + eta(n,h(v))n = h(v); and v = -eta(n,v)n + h(v) is unique because the two summands lie in span(n) and n^perp, which meet only in 0. (a) By def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, U = x'/tau' with tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(x',x')), so eta(U,U) = eta(x',x')/(tau')^2 = eta(x',x') c^2/(-eta(x',x')) = -c^2; timelikeness and the future direction of U follow from those of x' and positivity of 1/tau'. (b) eta(U,U) is the constant -c^2 along a C^2 worldline; differentiating componentwise in an eta-orthonormal basis with thm-algebra-of-derivatives gives 0 = (d/ds) eta(U,U) = 2 eta(U,U'), hence eta(U,U') = 0, and dividing by tau' > 0 gives eta(U,A) = 0. If A(s) is nonzero, then A(s) lies in (U(s)/c)^perp, a positive definite space by (c), so eta(A,A) > 0: A(s) is spacelike. (d) By (c), h(u) lies in n^perp and u = gamma n + h(u) with gamma = -eta(n,u). First, gamma > 0: in the inertial frame of (c), future timelikeness of n and u gives n^0 > |n_s| and u^0 > |u_s| (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components), so eta(n,u) = -n^0 u^0 + delta(n_s,u_s) <= -n^0 u^0 + |n_s||u_s| < 0. Second, eta(u,u) = gamma^2 eta(n,n) + eta(h(u),h(u)) = -gamma^2 + |h(u)|^2 = -1, so |h(u)|^2 = gamma^2 - 1 >= 0, giving gamma >= 1; substituting w = c h(u)/gamma gives |w|^2 = c^2 (gamma^2-1)/gamma^2 = c^2(1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, and solving for gamma gives gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2} and gamma = 1 iff h(u) = 0 iff u = n. (e) In the chart the coordinate path is t |-> (c t, r(t)), so x' = (c,w) and -eta(x',x') = c^2 - |w|^2 > 0 by future timelikeness, giving |w| < c and tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(c^2-|w|^2) = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{1/2} = 1/gamma_w; hence U = x'/tau' = gamma_w (c,w). For C^2 paths, d gamma_w/dt = gamma_w^3 (w.a)/c^2 by thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives (applied to the power -1/2) with the chain rule, and collecting terms in A = gamma_w dU/dt gives the displayed components; expanding eta(A,A) in the diagonal form and using gamma_w^2(1-|w|^2/c^2) = 1 gives eta(A,A) = gamma_w^4 |a|^2 + gamma_w^6 (w.a)^2/c^2 >= 0 with equality iff |a| = 0, and eta(U,A) = 0 agrees with (b). (f) The specialization n = e_0 is the evaluation h(u) = u - u^0 e_0 = (0, w/c gamma_w) and gamma = u^0 = gamma_w, so w_rel = w. No choice principle is used; all arguments are finite-dimensional or one-variable calculus.

current_affected_interface_subjects.current_statement: Statement refuted: 'if q lies in J^+(p) then q lies in I^+(p), i.e. every causally related pair of events can be joined by a future timelike worldline.' Counterexample: let p := x^{-1}(0,0,0,0) and q := x^{-1}(3,3,0,0) in the chart x of an inertial frame. Then D := q - p = (3,3,0,0) has eta(D,D) = -9 + 9 = 0 with D^0 = 3 > 0, so D is future null and q lies in J^+(p) but not in I^+(p) by the coordinate criterion; in particular the straight path from p to q is future null, not future timelike. Moreover no future timelike worldline y: [a,b] -> A with y(a) = p and y(b) = q exists: if it did, its displacement q - p would be future timelike by clause (a) of thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence, contradicting eta(D,D) = 0. The pair (p,q) is nonetheless causally related and the null straight segment realizes the relation, so the refuted statement is false.

Then x(0) = p, x(1) = p - d = q, and x'(s) = -d is past timelike for every s, so x is not a future timelike worldline; but its length integrand is sqrt(-eta(-d,-d)) = sqrt(-eta(d,d)) = 4 and its length integral over [0,1] equals 4, while sqrt(-eta(q-p,q-p)) = sqrt(-eta(-d,-d)) = 4: the bound is attained with equality by a past-directed parametrization. Attainment of the length bound therefore does not force the future time orientation; that orientation enters only through the model's clock interpretation, which attaches readings to future timelike worldlines (def-sr-proper-time, def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline). Within the future timelike worldline class the equality case is characterized by thm-sr-endpoint-proper-time-bound-and-flat-maximum (ii).

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], $c>0$, and let $n\in V$ be future unit, $\eta(n,n)=-1$, with rest space $n^\perp$, rest projection $h(v)=v+\eta(n,v)n$ and norm $|w|=\sqrt{\eta(w,w)}$ on $n^\perp$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c).
(a) For every $P$ in the future closed cone $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ define the observer energy of $P$ relative to $n$ by $E_n(P):=-c\,\eta(P,n)$, the observer spatial momentum by $q_n(P):=h(P)$, and, when $P$ is nonzero future causal, the invariant mass by $m(P):=\sqrt{-\eta(P,P)}/c$. Then $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$, $\eta(n,P)=-E_n(P)/c$, and $P=(E_n(P)/c)\,n+q_n(P)$ is the unique decomposition of $P$ as a multiple of $n$ plus a vector of $n^\perp$; equivalently $E_n$ and $q_n$ are the unique pair of a real number and a vector of $n^\perp$ with that property. For future null $P$ the same formula gives $m(P)=0$.
(b) If $m>0$ and $P$ is written as $P=mU$ with $U$ future timelike and $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ (the four-velocity normalisation of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]), call $m$ the rest-mass parameter of $P$, $mc^2$ its rest energy and $T_n(P):=E_n(P)-mc^2$ its kinetic energy relative to the observer $n$ and the parameter $m$. The kinetic energy is defined only after $m$ has been fixed, so it is not a function of $P$ and $n$ alone.
(c) The definition claims no positivity of $E_n$, no inequality or vanishing property of $T_n$, and no physical measurement. The names observer energy, spatial momentum, invariant mass, rest energy and kinetic energy and the units joule, kilogram metre per second and kilogram belong to the unit conventions of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]] and to the physical postulates of this framework; the mathematical content asserted here is only the explicit dependence of the four quantities on $P$, $n$ and $m$.
(d) $E_n$ and $q_n$ are functions of the pair $(P,n)$: $q_n(P)$ is an element of the vector space $V$, not a coordinate triple, and no basis of $V$ enters its definition; $m(P)$ depends on the scalar $\eta(P,P)$ alone; $T_n(P)$ depends additionally on the chosen real number $m$.

current_affected_interface_subjects.current_statement: Let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the affine Minkowski space and let n be a future unit timelike vector, eta(n,n) = -1. (a) Rest space. The rest space of n is the hyperplane n^perp = {v in V : eta(n,v) = 0}; by thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition (c) it is a three-dimensional linear subspace on which eta restricts to a positive-definite symmetric form, and the orthogonal projection onto it is h(v) = v + eta(n,v)n. (b) Simultaneity slice. For p in A the simultaneity slice of p relative to n is the affine hyperplane H(p,n) := p + n^perp = {q in A : eta(n,q-p) = 0}; it contains p and is three-dimensional, not a single point. (c) Simultaneity relation. Define q ~_n q' iff eta(n,q'-q) = 0, i.e. iff q'-q lies in n^perp. Then ~_n is an equivalence relation on A whose equivalence classes are exactly the slices H(p,n); reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity are consequences of n^perp being a linear subspace and not physical assumptions. (d) Rest distance. For p,q with q in H(p,n) define d_n(p,q) := sqrt(eta(q-p,q-p)). This is a real number >= 0, symmetric in p,q, vanishes exactly when p = q, and satisfies the triangle inequality on each slice, because the restriction of eta to n^perp is a positive-definite inner product. (e) Dependence on n and scope. The relation ~_n and the slices H(p,n) depend on the chosen future unit timelike n: an event q with eta(n,q-p) = 0 generally has eta(n',q-p) not equal to 0 for another future unit n' (an explicit witness is given on this page). Simultaneity here is defined relative to a prescribed observer vector and is not an absolute relation. For a congruence n(.) one may form the pointwise slices H(p,n(p)); whether these assemble into hypersurfaces is a separate integrability question settled below on this page, and no global foliation is asserted.

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model and $c>0$.
(a) For a finite list $(P_1,\dots,P_N)$, $N\ge0$, of vectors of $V$ define the total four-momentum $P_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\sum_{i=1}^NP_i$ as the finite sum of [[def-finite-sum-in-a-commutative-monoid]] in the additive group $(V,+)$; the empty sum is $0$.
(b) If $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future timelike, define its invariant mass $M:=M(P_{\mathrm{tot}}):=\sqrt{-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},P_{\mathrm{tot}})}/c>0$ and its rest energy $Mc^2$; if $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future null, set $M:=0$ and say that the system has no rest frame. For zero, spacelike or past $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ this convention defines no invariant mass.
(c) A center-of-momentum frame of a nonzero $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ whose first vector satisfies $q_{e_0}(P_{\mathrm{tot}})=0$, i.e. the total spatial momentum vanishes for the frame's stationary observer; by [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]] this is equivalent to $P_{\mathrm{tot}}=-\eta(P_{\mathrm{tot}},e_0)e_0$, that is, to $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ being a positive multiple of $e_0$.
(d) The invariant mass of a single future timelike vector $P$ coincides with $m(P)$ of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]]; in particular for $P=mU$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ it equals $m$.
(e) No existence of a center-of-momentum frame, no physical conservation law and no dynamics are asserted by this definition; position, event and simultaneity data do not enter $\sum_iP_i$, and only the total vector carries the invariant mass.

current_affected_interface_subjects.current_statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, $n$ future unit, and let $E_n,q_n,m,T_n$ be the quantities of [[def-sr-observed-energy-momentum-and-kinetic-energy]].
(a) If $P$ is nonzero future causal, then $E_n(P)>0$, $q_n(P)\in n^\perp$ and
$$\eta(q_n(P),q_n(P))=\frac{E_n(P)^2}{c^2}+\eta(P,P)\ \ge\ 0 .$$
Consequently: (i) if $P$ is future null then $\eta(P,P)=0$ and $E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$; (ii) if $P$ is future timelike with invariant mass $m(P)$ then $\eta(P,P)=-m(P)^2c^2$ and the mass-shell identity
$$E_n(P)^2=m(P)^2c^4+c^2\,|q_n(P)|^2$$
holds. The invariant mass $m(P)$ does not depend on the observer $n$ or on coordinates, being a function of the scalar $\eta(P,P)$ alone, while $E_n$ and $q_n$ do depend on $n$.
(b) Let $P=mU$ with $m>0$ constant and $U$ future timelike, $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. With $\gamma:=-\eta(U/c,n)\ge1$ and $w:=c\,h(U)/\gamma\in n^\perp$ the relative velocity of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d), one has
$$E_n(P)=mc^2\gamma,\qquad T_n(P)=mc^2(\gamma-1)\ \ge\ 0,\qquad q_n(P)=m\gamma w,$$
and $m(P)=m$. Moreover $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if $\gamma=1$, that is $U=cn$, equivalently $P=mcn$ (the particle is at rest relative to $n$). Finally $|q_n(P)|=m\gamma|w|=mc\sqrt{\gamma^2-1}$.
current_affected_interface_subjects.current_strategy: All clauses are algebra in the flat model. (a) Expand $q_n(P)=P+\eta(P,n)n$: bilinearity and $\eta(n,n)=-1$ give $\eta(q_n,q_n)=\eta(P,P)+\eta(P,n)^2$, and $\eta(P,n)=-E_n(P)/c$. Positivity of $E_n$: choose an $\eta$-orthonormal basis with first vector in $C^+$ ([[lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis]], [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]]) and write $P=P^0e_0+P_s$, $n=n^0e_0+n_s$; then $n^0>|n_s|$ and $P^0\ge|P_s|$ by [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], so $-\eta(P,n)=P^0n^0-P_s\cdot n_s\ge n^0|P_s|-|n_s|\,|P_s|=|P_s|(n^0-|n_s|)\ge0$ using the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite]], [[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]); equality forces $P_s=0$, and then $P\ne0$ gives $P^0>0$ and $-\eta(P,n)=P^0n^0>0$. Substitute $\eta(P,P)=-m(P)^2c^2$ for (ii). (b) From $u:=U/c=\gamma(n+w/c)$ of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(d) one gets $q_n(P)=mc\,h(u)=m\gamma w$ and $E_n(P)=-mc\,\eta(U,n)=mc^2(-\eta(U/c,n))=mc^2\gamma$; the rest is the identity $|w|^2=c^2(1-\gamma^{-2})$ and $\gamma\ge1$ from the same item, with $\gamma=1$ if and only if $u=n$. No choice principle is used.

current_affected_interface_subjects.current_statement: Let n be a future unit timelike vector, eta(n,n) = -1, let o be an event, and let lambda_- < lambda_+ be real numbers; put e_- := o + lambda_- n and e_+ := o + lambda_+ n. In that case q - e_- = ((lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2) n + u and e_+ - q = ((lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2) n - u, the affine midpoint m := o + ((lambda_- + lambda_+)/2) n = (e_- + e_+)/2 satisfies eta(n,q-m) = 0 (so q lies in the slice H(m,n)) and |q - m| = (lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2. Then q = o + ((lambda_- + lambda_+)/2) n + h(d) with u := h(d) in n^perp and |u| = (lambda_+ - lambda_-)/2. current_affected_interface_subjects.current_statement: Consider the following hypothetical signalling model in the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (A,V,eta,C^+) with the SI coordinate conventions x^0 = c t (def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions). (S1) There are transmitters, each at rest in an inertial frame, that emit localized signals travelling at a fixed speed u with u > c in that frame, in any spatial direction. (S2) A received signal can be immediately re-emitted at the same event by a receiver, at speed u in the receiver's own rest frame (unrestricted receiving and relaying, no delay, no loss). (S3) Transmitters and receivers may move inertially at any speed v with 0 < v < c. (S4) The displacement between the emission and the reception event of a signal is a vector of the affine model, and displacements transform between inertial charts by the model's Lorentz transitions; the framework's kinematics is not modified. Then there is an explicit configuration in which a one-relay signal chain is received strictly before it was emitted: let L > 0, 0 < v < c and u > c satisfy v > 2u/(1 + u^2/c^2), which is possible because 2u/(1 + u^2/c^2) < c for u > c; let A rest at x^1 = 0 in an inertial chart x and let B move with the straight worldline x^1 = L + vt; emit a signal from A at the event A_0 = x^{-1}(0,0,0,0), in the direction of increasing x^1; let B receive it at the event B_1 and re-emit immediately toward A at speed u in B's rest frame. Then the following are exact identities of the model. (a) t(B_1) = L/(u - v) > 0 and x^1(B_1) = uL/(u - v) > 0, and the displacement B_1 - A_0 = (c t(B_1), x^1(B_1), 0, 0) is spacelike. (b) The return displacement in the chart x is (c Delta t, -x^1(B_1), 0, 0) with Delta t = x^1(B_1)(1 - vu/c^2)/(u - v), which is negative under the stated choice of v, and the arrival event A_1 on A's worldline satisfies t(A_1) = t(B_1) + Delta t = L(2u - v - v u^2/c^2)/(u - v)^2 < 0. (c) Hence A_1 - A_0 = (c t(A_1),0,0,0) with t(A_1) < 0, so A_1 lies in the strict chronological past I^-(A_0) of the emission event, and the return displacement B_1 - A_1 is spacelike. (d) In the model S1-S4 a signal chain therefore connects an emission event A_0 to an event A_1 in the strict past of A_0, and each leg's reception is spacelike-separated from its emission; by (c) of thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence the composition of the two legs is incompatible with the causal signal restriction post-sr-causal-signal-propagation, under which a reception event of a transmission lies in the causal future of its emission event and a relay chain cannot return to its own emission event (pthm-sr-causal-signal-order-and-composition(ii)-(iii)). So the hypothetical model S1-S4 and the causal signal restriction cannot both describe one and the same process family. (e) Scope and qualification. current_affected_interface_subjects.current_statement: Let Omega be a nonempty open subset of A. (i) Flow box. If X is a smooth vector field on Omega and X(p) is nonzero at a point p of Omega, then there is an open neighbourhood U of p in Omega and a chart (u^0,u^1,u^2,u^3): U -> R^4 in which X = partial/partial u^0; the integral curves of X in U are therefore the u^0-coordinate lines up to reparametrization. In particular every observer congruence n on Omega admits a local n-adapted chart, and in such a chart n = partial/partial u^0. (ii) Frobenius criterion. For a smooth nowhere-zero one-form alpha on Omega let D := ker alpha be the hyperplane distribution D_p = {v in V : alpha_p(v) = 0}. Then D is integrable on Omega (through every point there passes a local hypersurface whose tangent space at each of its points is the corresponding D_p) if and only if alpha wedge d alpha = 0 on Omega. (iii) Rest distributions of observer congruences. Let n be an observer congruence on Omega, alpha := n-flat, and let theta, omega be its expansion and vorticity (definition of the congruence kinematics). Then: (a) d alpha = 2 nabla_{[a}n_{b]}, i.e. d alpha(X,Y) = (nabla_X n-flat)(Y) - (nabla_Y n-flat)(X) for smooth vector fields X,Y; (b) for every p and all X,Y with alpha(X) = alpha(Y) = 0 one has d alpha(X,Y) = 2 omega(X,Y); consequently (alpha wedge d alpha)(p) = 0 if and only if omega(p) = 0, and on an open set U contained in Omega the following are equivalent: alpha wedge d alpha = 0 on U, omega = 0 on U, and the rest distribution ker alpha is integrable on U; (c) when the rest distribution is integrable on U, its integral hypersurfaces are orthogonal to n at every point and the restriction of eta to each of them is positive definite, so they are rest slices of the congruence. All statements are local on Omega; no global foliation, global synchronization, completeness or product structure is asserted, and no claim is made about variable-rank or non-smooth distributions.

current_affected_interface_subjects.current_statement: Statement refuted: "The four-momentum of an ideal massless particle is obtained by setting $m=0$ in $P=mU$, where $U$ is a future timelike four-velocity with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$." For every future timelike $U$ one has $0\cdot U=0$, and $0$ is not a nonzero future null vector: it is not null (null means $\eta(P,P)=0$ with $P\ne0$) and it has zero energy relative to every observer, $E_n(0)=0$. Conversely, a nonzero future null vector such as $P=(E/c)(e_0+e_1)$, $E>0$, in the first two vectors of an inertial frame satisfies $\eta(P,P)=0$, $E_{e_0}(P)=E>0$, but is not of the form $mU$ with $m>0$ (such a vector is future timelike) or $m=0$ (which gives $0\ne P$). Hence no value of $m\ge0$ produces $P$ by the formula $mU$: a massless momentum is a separate model primitive, and the degenerate case $m=0$ of the massive formula carries no information about it.

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model and $c>0$.
(a) A collision datum is a triple $(p;(P_1,\dots,P_N);(P'_1,\dots,P'_K))$ consisting of an event $p\in A$, a finite nonempty list of incoming vectors in $V$ and a finite nonempty list of outgoing vectors in $V$, with side totals $Q_{\mathrm{in}}:=\sum_{i=1}^NP_i$ and $Q_{\mathrm{out}}:=\sum_{j=1}^KP'_j$ formed as in [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]; the datum conserves if $Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$. Two-sided data may be compared only through these totals.
(b) A leg $P$ is massive with mass $m>0$ if $P=mU$ for some future timelike $U$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, and null if $P$ is a nonzero future null vector. A datum is on-shell if every leg is massive with a recorded mass or null; a mass-specified datum records the mass $m>0$ of each massive leg or the value $0$ for each null leg. The mass sum of a side is the sum of the recorded positive masses of its massive legs; a side is massive-only if all its legs are massive.
(c) A datum is causal if every leg lies in $\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$; two-leg if both sides have two legs; equal-mass if in addition both sides are two-leg and the recorded masses agree pair by pair.
(d) The definition is purely mathematical: it neither asserts that any datum describes a physical process, nor that a conserving datum exists for a prescribed list of legs, nor any law of nature. Position, simultaneity, mechanism and interaction strength are not part of a datum; only the event, the two finite lists and their recorded masses are.

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $Q$ be a future timelike vector with invariant mass $M:=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$; put $n_Q:=Q/(Mc)$, so that $\eta(n_Q,n_Q)=-1$, $n_Q\in C^+$ and $Q=Mc\,n_Q$.
(a) There exists an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with $e_0=n_Q$; in every such frame $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$, $E_{e_0}(Q)=Mc^2$ and the components of $Q$ are $(Mc,0,0,0)$. Such a frame is a center-of-momentum frame of $Q$ in the sense of [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]]\,(c).
(b) Conversely, if an inertial frame satisfies $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$, then $e_0=n_Q$. Hence the time vector of a center-of-momentum frame of $Q$ is unique, and two center-of-momentum frames of $Q$ differ only by the choice of origin and by a positively oriented $\eta$-orthonormal change of the spatial basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $n_Q^\perp$; in particular the center-of-momentum frame is unique up to spatial rotations.
(c) If $Q$ is a nonzero future null vector, then no inertial frame satisfies $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$: a nonzero future null vector has no center-of-momentum frame.
current_affected_interface_subjects.current_strategy: Existence: $n_Q$ is future unit. By [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]\,(c) the restriction of $\eta$ to $n_Q^\perp$ is positive definite, so by [[cor-finite-dimensional-inner-product-spaces-have-orthonormal-bases]] choose an orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of $n_Q^\perp$ for the restricted inner product; then $(n_Q,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\eta$-orthonormal, and if its orientation class is negative replace $e_1$ by $-e_1$ ([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]), which preserves orthonormality and the first vector; [[lem-future-oriented-inertial-frames-exist]] and [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] give an inertial frame with this basis. Then $q_{e_0}(Q)=h(Q)=Q+\eta(Q,n_Q)n_Q=Q-Mc\,n_Q=0$ and $E_{e_0}(Q)=-c\eta(Q,n_Q)=Mc^2$. Uniqueness: $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$ says $Q=-\eta(Q,e_0)e_0$ with $-\eta(Q,e_0)>0$ ([[lem-sr-energy-momentum-observer-identities]]\,(a) applied to the single vector $Q$), so $Q$ is a positive multiple of $e_0$; comparing with $Q=Mc\,n_Q$ and $\eta(e_0,e_0)=-1$ gives $e_0=n_Q$. The remaining freedom is the spatial basis of $e_0^\perp=n_Q^\perp$, which must be positively oriented and $\eta$-orthonormal. (c) $q_{e_0}(Q)=0$ would again exhibit $Q$ as a nonzero multiple of the timelike vector $e_0$, contradicting nullity. No choice principle is used (the orthonormal basis is obtained by finite Gram-Schmidt over the positive definite $n_Q^\perp$).

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model and $c>0$.
(a) If $v,w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$ then $v+w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$; if in addition $v\in C^+$ or $w\in C^+$, then $v+w\in C^+$. Moreover $-\eta(v,w)\ge0$ for $v,w\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$, with equality if and only if $v=0$, or $w=0$, or both $v$ and $w$ are future null and parallel (equivalently $w=\lambda v$ for some $\lambda\ge0$).
(b) If $P_1,\dots,P_N$ with $N\ge1$ are nonzero future causal vectors, then $P_{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_{i=1}^NP_i$ is a nonzero future causal vector; if at least one $P_i$ is future timelike, then $P_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is future timelike. The converse implication does not hold: two future null vectors that are not parallel have a future timelike sum.
(c) For every future unit $n$ and all $P_1,\dots,P_N\in\mathrm{cl}(C^+)$,

Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski model, $c>0$, and let $\mathcal D=(p;(P_1,\dots,P_N);(P'_1,\dots,P'_K))$ be a mass-specified conserving collision datum of [[def-sr-collision-datum-and-conservation]], causal and on-shell, all of whose legs are nonzero; write $Q:=Q_{\mathrm{in}}=Q_{\mathrm{out}}$.
(a) If $Q$ is future timelike with invariant mass $M$, then $M$ is the common invariant mass of both sides, $Q$ has the center-of-momentum frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ of [[lem-sr-center-of-momentum-frame]], and in that frame
$$Mc^2=\sum_{\text{legs of a side}}E_{e_0}(\text{leg})\qquad\text{for each side};$$
each massive leg $\ell=mU$ has $E_{e_0}(\ell)=mc^2\gamma_\ell\ge mc^2$ with equality if and only if $U=ce_0$, and each null leg has $E_{e_0}>0$. Hence for each side $S\in\{\mathrm{in},\mathrm{out}\}$,
$$M\ \ge\ \sum_{\text{massive legs }\ell\in S}m_\ell,$$
with equality if and only if $S$ is massive-only and every massive leg of $S$ has four-velocity $ce_0$ (all massive particles of that side at rest in the center-of-momentum frame).
(b) If $Q$ is future null, then every leg is null, all legs are mutually parallel in one null direction, $M=0$ by the convention of [[def-sr-total-four-momentum-and-invariant-mass]], and no center-of-momentum frame exists.
(c) Suppose the incoming side is two-leg, $P_i=m_iU_i$ with $m_i>0$, and put $n_2:=U_2/c$ (the future unit observer comoving with the second leg), $\gamma:=-\eta(U_1/c,n_2)\ge1$ and $E:=E_{n_2}(P_1)=m_1c^2\gamma$. Then
$$M^2=m_1^2+m_2^2+\frac{2m_2E}{c^2}.$$
Consequently, if the outgoing side is mass-specified with massive masses $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_L$, $L\ge1$ (it may also contain null legs), the datum can conserve only if
$$E\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{l=1}^L\mu_l\Bigr)^2-m_1^2-m_2^2\Bigr],\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad T:=E-m_1c^2\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{l=1}^L\mu_l\Bigr)^2-(m_1+m_2)^2\Bigr].$$
(d) [null legs] If $P_1,P_2$ are future null and there is an inertial frame with $P_i=(E_i/c)(e_0+s_i)$, $E_i>0$, $s_1,s_2$ unit spatial vectors with $s_2=-s_1$, then $Q$ is future timelike and $M=2\sqrt{E_1E_2}/c^2$. More generally, with $s_1,s_2$ unit vectors making Euclidean angle $\theta\in[0,\pi]$, $Q$ is future timelike for $\theta\ne0$ with
$$M=\frac{\sqrt{2E_1E_2(1-\cos\theta)}}{c^2},$$
while for $\theta=0$ the total $Q$ is future null, $M=0$ and no center-of-momentum frame exists. In particular, a conserving on-shell collision datum whose incoming side is a single null leg and whose outgoing side contains at least one massive leg does not exist.
(e) All clauses are conditional implications from the hypotheses of a conserving, causal, on-shell datum. They assert no interaction, no existence of a conservation process for prescribed legs, no cross section, amplitude or probability, and no empirical fact.

Adopt [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]] and [[post-sr-ideal-massless-particle-momentum]]. Then the following conditional physical claims hold in the flat classical model, with the units of [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]].
(a) Massive particle. Let a massive particle have constant mass $m>0$, four-momentum $P=mU$ and a future unit observer $n$. Its measured energy $E_n(P)=-c\eta(P,n)$, spatial momentum $q_n(P)=h(P)$ and kinetic energy $T_n(P)=E_n(P)-mc^2$ satisfy $E_n(P)>0$, $T_n(P)\ge0$ and the mass-shell identity $E_n(P)^2=m^2c^4+c^2|q_n(P)|^2$; $T_n(P)=0$ if and only if the particle is at rest in the observer's frame ($U=cn$). In an inertial frame whose stationary observer is $n=e_0$, the components are $P=(E/c,\mathbf p)$ with $E=E_{e_0}(P)=m\gamma_wc^2$ and $\mathbf p=q_{e_0}(P)=m\gamma_w\mathbf w$ for the coordinate velocity $\mathbf w$, and under a passive boost the components transform as the components of the vector $P$; the combination $E^2-c^2|\mathbf p|^2=m^2c^4$ is frame-independent.
(b) Four-force. Along a $C^2$ worldline with four-acceleration $A$, the four-force $F=\dot P$ satisfies $\eta(P,F)=0$ and $F=mA$; in an inertial frame $F=\gamma\,(\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w/c,\mathbf f)$ and $dE/dt=\mathbf f\cdot\mathbf w$, where $\mathbf f=d\mathbf p/dt$ is the coordinate three-force. The constancy of $m$ is used; if instead $m$ is a $C^1$ variable mass parameter, then $\eta(P,F)=-mc^2\,dm/d\tau$, and the constant-mass identities are not transferred to variable-mass systems.
(c) System mass. For a finite nonempty system of particles all of whose four-momenta are nonzero future causal and whose total four-momentum $Q$ is future timelike, the invariant mass $M=\sqrt{-\eta(Q,Q)}/c$ satisfies: in the center-of-momentum frame with $e_0=Q/(Mc)$ one has $Mc^2=\sum_iE_{e_0}(P_i)$; every massive constituent has $E_{e_0}(P_i)\ge m_ic^2$, with equality exactly when it is at rest in that frame, and every massless constituent has $E_{e_0}(P_i)>0$. Hence $M\ge\sum_im_i$ over the massive constituents, with equality if and only if the system is massive-only and all its constituents are at rest in the center-of-momentum frame. If $Q$ is future null, then $M=0$, all constituents are massless with parallel momenta, and no center-of-momentum frame exists.
(d) Massless particle. An ideal massless particle has $E_n(P)=c\,|q_n(P)|>0$, has no rest frame and is not $mU$ for any $m>0$; it is not obtained from the massive formula by setting $m=0$.
(e) Necessary collision thresholds. Suppose that, under the adopted isolated-collision balance, an isolated collision occurs whose incoming legs are massive particles of constant masses $m_1,\dots,m_N$ and whose outgoing legs are massive particles of masses $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_K$ and possibly ideal massless particles. Let $M$ be the invariant mass of the common total four-momentum $Q$ when $Q$ is future timelike. Then the necessary inequalities $M\ge\sum_im_i$ and $M\ge\sum_j\mu_j$ hold; if the incoming side is a projectile of mass $m_1$ and a target of mass $m_2$ at rest in the observer frame of the target, with projectile energy $E$ and kinetic energy $T=E-m_1c^2$ in that frame, then
$$E\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^K\mu_j\Bigr)^2-m_1^2-m_2^2\Bigr],\qquad T\ \ge\ \frac{c^2}{2m_2}\Bigl[\Bigl(\sum_{j=1}^K\mu_j\Bigr)^2-(m_1+m_2)^2\Bigr],$$
and a single incoming massless particle cannot collide into an outgoing state containing a massive particle. These are kinematic necessity statements under the adopted conservation: they do not assert that any collision occurs, do not fix probabilities, amplitudes or cross sections, and are not empirical findings.
(f) Scope. All clauses are conditional on the two postulates and on the stated idealisations; the conclusions carry the same idealisations. No measurement, precision, statistical or empirical claim is made.
